title: Salade Niçoise
subtitle: Tuna, egg, and vegetable salad from Nice
excerpt: A composed salad of tuna, hard-boiled eggs, green beans, tomatoes, olives, anchovy, and new potatoes, dressed simply with olive oil and wine vinegar. No lettuce beneath it all.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salade niçoise is the definitive dish of Nice and the Côte d'Azur. The classic version, as defended by the city of Nice itself, is strictly raw vegetables only: no cooked potatoes, no cooked green beans. But the version that spread across France, Britain, and the world in the 20th century includes briefly cooked new potatoes and green beans, which most people prefer for texture and substance. The tuna should be the best quality available: good tinned tuna in olive oil, or seared fresh tuna. The dressing is a simple vinaigrette. The anchovies are optional but give the proper Niçoise punch.

content.text: Dress each component separately before assembling rather than tossing everything together: this keeps the salad distinct rather than merged. Do not overdress; the components should be coated lightly, not swimming in vinaigrette. The salad is arranged on the plate, not tossed in a bowl: it is a composed salad.

Cook the potatoes in salted boiling water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and halve while warm. Blanch the green beans in boiling salted water for 3 minutes until just tender but still bright green. Drain and refresh in cold water.
Whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, mustard, and salt to make the dressing.

Arrange the potatoes, green beans, tomatoes, olives, and tuna on a large platter. Nestle the egg halves in. Lay the anchovy fillets across the salad. Drizzle the dressing over everything. Serve at room temperature.
